To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elevation of intracellular cAMP levels in normal rat kidney cells potentiates lysosomal exocytic fusion triggered by Ca2+.

(i) elevation in intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) potentiates the exocytosis induced by calcium of lysosomes in rat fibroblasts; and that (ii) cAMP is also involved in the invasion by Trypanosome cruzi, a parasite that triggers calcium-dependent lysosomal exocytic events.
cAMP regulates Ca2+-dependent fusion of lysosomes with the host cell plasma membrane, a process required for parasite entry into the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Ca2+-dependent cell invasion by T. cruzi and the role of Ca2+-regulated lysosomal exocytic pathways in this process.
the role of cAMP in Ca2+-dependent processes that are important to the biology of the cell and the parasite.
the regulation of Ca2+-regulated secretion, a ubiquitous process that has been implicated in the regulation of diverse biological functions, including cell invasion by parasites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cAMP regulates Ca2+-dependent cell invasion by T. cruzi through modulation of Ca2+-inducible lysosomal exocytic events.
cAMP regulates Ca2+-dependent vesicle exocytosis in a variety of cells.
the cAMP-dependent protein kinase is an important regulator of the exocytosis process, which is involved in the invasion of the host cell by T. cruzi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cAMP is involved in the regulation of lysosomal exocytic events in a cell-type and parasite-dependent manner.
cAMP regulates the Ca2+-dependent release of lysosomal contents in normal rat kidney cells, and this process is important for T. cruzI cell invasion.
the cAMP signaling pathway modulates Ca2+-regulated lysosomal exocytic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+-dependent fusion events can be regulated by a second messenger, cAMP, which can be modulated in a G-protein-dependent way.
cAMP can regulate Ca2+-dependent fusion of lysosomes with the cell membrane.
cAMP regulates Ca2+-dependent fusion of lysosomes with the cell plasma membrane and that the process can be triggered by a parasite/host cell interplay.
